title: Add a reviewable Jev decision gate to a LangChain agent
description: Build an agent harness that checks proposed tool calls, preserves human approval, and records uncertain Jev decisions.

guide_authors.name: Appit Studio
guide_authors.role: Editorial guide; AI-assisted drafting and implementation

connections.step: Compare a separate MCP/hook screening layer with the LangChain middleware path
connections.why: Screens tool calls and results through a proxy or hooks, with shadow mode and policy thresholds; useful when the agent is not a LangChain application.
connections.limitations: Apache-2.0 source; live screening sends selected tool content to TypeSafe and can incur charges. Shadow mode blocks nothing. Not a sandbox or a substitute for approval.

connections.step: Explore model selection after the tool gate works
connections.why: Filters eligible coding-agent models with deterministic quota and policy rules before Jev ranks a route; it illustrates the article's model-routing idea outside LangChain.
connections.limitations: MIT pre-release CLI; live use requires TypeSafe and a supported agent login, and Herdr for launches. It routes coding-agent runs, not arbitrary LangChain model calls.

connections.step: Practice keeping typed judgments separate from deterministic actions
connections.why: Its offline fixtures show a complete request, response, review queue and failure policy before any live provider call.
connections.limitations: MIT repository example, not a community project record; synthetic fixtures do not measure Jev accuracy or tool safety.

faqs.question: Does Auto Mode ask a person to approve a risky call?
faqs.answer: No. The documented middleware refuses risky calls; use a separate approval flow when a person must decide. Keep explicit permissions in code.

faqs.question: Can I rely on a Jev probability as proof that a tool call is safe?
faqs.answer: No. Typed output constrains shape, not correctness. Evaluate false allows and false blocks on representative traces, and maintain sandbox and permission boundaries.

faqs.question: Must I install all linked projects?
faqs.answer: No. The primary recipe uses LangChain's TypeSafe integration. Agent Chaperone is an alternative screening layer; Agent Router addresses model choice; Support Router demonstrates an offline decision-policy pattern.
